label: original-phase bigram: y/a/q/c input after a/c/t/y/v/w
explanation: Fires almost only during the original (input) phase (95% of mass), mostly at positions 1-6, and depends on both the current and the previous input token, like a bigram detector. Current token: y gives 55% of mass (active on 15% of y steps), then a (21%), q (16%), c (5%), t (2%). It is strongly boosted when the previous token is a, c, t, y, v or w. The largest activations are y right after a or c (e.g. "a a y", "c y", "a c y"). On its own the current token is too weak a signal (precision about 0.2); adding the previous-token condition raises precision to about 0.55, at the cost of some recall. Never fires at t=0, at the delimiter, or on most other letters and digits; copy-phase activations are rare (5% of mass). It fires slightly more in sequences with fewer digits. The response looks graded over token pairs, so a boolean predicate only captures it roughly.
